title: Extension by zero on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, extension by zero on the small pro-etale
site (the functor $j_!$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero])
is the exact left adjoint of $j^{-1}$, acts degreewise, and
has the same stalk prescription as the etale one,

$$
(j_!K)_{\bar x}=
\begin{cases}
K_{\bar x},&\bar x\text{ lies in }U,\\
0,&\bar x\text{ lies in }X\setminus U,
\end{cases}
$$

for a complex $K$ of sheaves of $A$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and a geometric point
$\bar x$ of $X$; it is compatible with restriction of scalars
along a homomorphism $A\to B$ of finite commutative rings [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]: canonically $\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}j_!^B K\cong j_!^A\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}K$ for a complex $K$ of $B$-module sheaves.

proof.text: Use the recorded openImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction and existing finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation instances for fixed A-module sheaves. Map the adjunction to cochain complexes using Adjunction.mapHomologicalComplex.

For y in U, use StructuredArrow.map2 to include its pointed neighbourhoods into those of y composed with j. This functor is fully faithful; refining any target neighbourhood by fibre product with U supplies an arrow from its image. Hence it is initial. The opposite functor is final and Final.colimIso identifies the restriction stalk with the ambient stalk naturally in every sheaf. The invertible unit of the open-immersion adjunction then gives the stalk isomorphism for extension by zero.

The outside-open module-sheaf stalk vanishes by lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-outside-stalk. Apply this statement to every term of a complex; the identity map of the stalk complex is degreewise zero, so the complex is a zero object.

Lift ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj to sheaf categories with sheafComposeAdjunction. The mate of the identity square for coextension and restriction along j is the identity square for scalar restriction, by the coefficient adjunction triangle identity on every section. Iterating mates identifies openExtensionScalarMap with the conjugate of the identity on the composite right adjoints. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms, so this precise canonical map is invertible. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to obtain the complex comparison.
Use Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso to extend the inside-open natural isomorphism to cochain complexes and combine all conjuncts.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtale_extension_by_zero (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j) ∧
    PreservesFiniteColimits (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j) ∧
    Nonempty (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j ⊣
      openImmersionRestriction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j) ∧
    Nonempty (openExtensionCochain A j ⊣
      (openImmersionRestriction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)) ∧
    (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U),
      Nonempty (openExtensionCochain A j ⋙
          (geometricModuleStalkFunctor A (y ≫ j)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
        (geometricModuleStalkFunctor A y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))) ∧
    (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X),
      (¬ ∃ z : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U, z ≫ j = y) →
      ∀ K : CochainComplex (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) ℤ,
        IsZero (((geometricModuleStalkFunctor A y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          ((openExtensionCochain A j).obj K))) ∧
    (∀ (B : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing B] [Finite B] (φ : A →+* B),
      IsIso (openExtensionScalarMap φ j) ∧
      IsIso ((openExtensionScalarMap φ j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)))
